**5B.10 Assessment**
Overall, **no**. Hasina’s government did make some genuine stabilization and infrastructure moves in 2024, but the economy did **not** end the year on a clearly stronger trajectory than it inherited. The positive side is mostly reform intent and partial correction under stress; the negative side includes inflation, reserve loss, external imbalance, weak job creation, rising poverty/inequality, and regime collapse.

**Accepted Claims**
- **IMF Executive Board Concludes the Second Review under the ECF/EFF/RSF for Bangladesh** | IMF | June 24, 2024 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/24/pr24234-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2nd-review-ecf-eff-rsf) | Claim: Bangladesh had already realigned its exchange rate and was taking corrective macro steps, which is the best positive evidence for an evidence-based stabilization trajectory. Still, the IMF also described major vulnerabilities, so this is reform in progress rather than a strong turnaround. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.7

- **Bangladesh Receives $900 million World Bank Financing to Increase Economic and Urban Resilience for Sustainable Growth** | World Bank | June 21, 2024 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth) | Claim: the government secured support for fiscal and financial-sector reforms, tax changes, procurement reform, and resilience spending. That is real positive evidence for longer-run trajectory, but it is still mostly reform design rather than proven outcome. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.7, 5B.4

- **World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities, and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities** | World Bank | May 28, 2024 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co) | Claim: Bangladesh and partners funded health, nutrition, education, roads, shelters, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities. This is a real positive under external constraint, showing targeted resilience investment in a severe humanitarian shock. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024** | UNFPA Bangladesh | 2024 | [URL](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024) | Claim: UNFPA delivered targeted services to women, girls, indigenous communities, transgender people, sex workers, and disaster-affected areas after climate shocks. This supports a limited positive reading for shock response and inclusion, but it is partner-led and not strong proof of Hasina’s own management success. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth** | World Bank | April 2, 2024 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r) | Claim: even in a favorable-growth environment, the Bank said inflation, BOP deficits, reserve pressure, import restrictions, and banking stress were eroding purchasing power and investment. This is the clearest evidence that the inherited situation was still deteriorating under Hasina’s stewardship. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.9

- **Factbox: Troubled Bangladesh’s economy bogged down by high unemployment, inflation** | Reuters | August 8, 2024 | [URL](https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1) | Claim: under Hasina, Bangladesh saw widening external deficits, taka depreciation, falling reserves, IMF dependence, and stagnant job creation. This is strong negative evidence that 2024 left the economy weaker, not stronger, despite external constraints. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.9

- **Bangladesh Army Enforces Curfew as Student-Led Protests Spiral** | Reuters | July 20, 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) | Claim: the government responded to the July crisis with curfew, office closures, army deployment, and communications disruption after deadly violence. That is evidence of crisis escalation and institutional damage, not a stronger trajectory. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.7

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina Blames Opposition for Violence, Curfew to Remain** | Reuters | July 22, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) | Claim: Hasina blamed political opponents for the violence and kept the curfew in place instead of pivoting to correction. This is direct scapegoating and weak evidence of competent crisis management. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.7

- **Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024** | World Bank | October 1, 2024 | [URL](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672) | Claim: the Bank projected slower growth, rising extreme poverty, and more than one Gini point of higher inequality, with jobs and revenue mobilization still unresolved. That undercuts any claim that 2024 left Bangladesh on a clearly stronger, fairer, or more stable trajectory. | QIDs: 5B.10, 5B.8, 5B.9

**Search Gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of sanctions relief or sanctions shock management, so the comparison mainly turns on inflation, reserves, jobs, debt/IMF dependence, climate shock response, and the July political crisis.
- The best positives are mainly **repair efforts under external pressure** and **partner-led resilience projects**, not clear evidence that Hasina herself left the economy stronger than she inherited it.
